rows.b: A future machine whose transistors switch at terahertz rates — a thousand times today's gigahertz. SPECULATION: no complete terahertz computer exists.
An experimental approach where quantum information is stored in the braided paths of exotic particles, protected from noise by topology itself. It is still laboratory research.
Individual charged atoms float in electromagnetic traps, and lasers flip their quantum states. Ions of the same kind are perfectly identical, which makes them excellent qubits.
A complete home computer sold through Radio Shack stores with keyboard, screen, and cassette storage. Ordinary families could buy one off the shelf.
One of the first computers built with transistors instead of vacuum tubes, which made it far smaller and cooler. It gave hackers a machine they could use directly, one at a time.
